The console, and the three things procurement asks first

Screens 1–3 and 14. Dr Camille Laurent evaluates on governance model, audit logs and SSO readiness, and buys a 1–3 lab pilot before wider rollout. That sequence is the design: the pilot dashboard is a first-class screen, not a trial banner, because the pilot is the thing being sold.

THE LEAVER CASE · WHERE MOST PLATFORMS LOSE THE DATA
T. Adeyemi · contract ended 2026-09-08 · deprovisioned automatically at 02:00.
Access revoked · sessions terminated · seat released
Institutional artifacts retained and reassigned to the PI
Handover pack generated and sent to the PI
Personal profile, ORCID and reputation travel with them
The split is the whole answer to "tacit knowledge leaves when researchers leave": the work stays with the institution, the identity stays with the person. Neither is negotiable at deprovisioning time — it is decided by policy, in advance.
MOVERS
A department change updates the affiliation and the lab membership but never re-scopes existing artifacts. Data does not silently follow a person into a new group — that requires an explicit transfer, logged.
Dry-run mode. Every sync can be previewed against live HR data with no writes, and the diff is downloadable. IT will not connect SCIM to a new vendor without this.

CRITERION 1MET
Onboarding time for a new lab member
9 dwas 6 weeks
target ≤ 2 weeks
Measured from account creation to first independent experiment. The onboarding checklist and existing method cards do the work.
CRITERION 2MET
Internal reuse rate
41%of artifacts reused by
someone who did not make them
Baseline was unmeasurable — the institution had no way to observe reuse before. That itself is a finding.
CRITERION 3PARTIAL
Audit readiness
2 of 3mock audits passed
without manual assembly
The third failed on pre-2026 work that predates the tenant. Nothing can fix that retrospectively, and the report says so rather than hiding it.
ADOPTION · BY LAB, HONESTLY
Krieger group · 11 people10 of 11 weekly
Van Damme group · 20 people7 of 20 weekly
The second lab is the real finding. Adoption tracks whether the PI uses it, not whether the tool is good — in the Van Damme group the PI has logged in twice. Shown prominently because a renewal decision made on the 91% number alone would be a mistake.
